t.5.21.1: Having spoken thus to Maithilī, King Rāvaṇa, who makes his enemies cry out, then gave orders to all the rākṣasīs and departed.
t.5.21.2: But when the lord of the rākṣasas had departed and gone back into the inner apartments, those rākṣasīs of terrible form rushed together upon Sītā.
t.5.21.4: O Sītā, you do not value highly the position of wife to the great-souled Rāvaṇa, the most excellent descendant of Pulastya, the ten-necked one.
t.5.21.3: Then the rākṣasīs, overcome with rage, approached Sītā and, in harsh words, spoke this further to Vaidehī:
t.5.21.5: Then the rākṣasī named Ekajaṭā, her eyes copper-red with anger, addressed Sītā, whose waist was slender as the palm of a hand, and spoke these words.
t.5.21.6: He who is the fourth among the six Prajāpatis, the mind-born son of Brahmā, is renowned as Pulastya.
t.5.21.7: The mind-born son of Pulastya was a radiant great sage, Viśravas by name, equal in splendor to Prajāpati.
t.5.21.8: His son, O large-eyed one, is Rāvaṇa, who makes his enemies cry out; you ought to become the wife of that lord of the Rākṣasas. O you whose every limb is lovely, why do you not assent to the words spoken by me?
t.5.21.10: You ought to become the wife of that lord of the Rākṣasas, by whom the thirty-three gods and the king of the gods were conquered.
t.5.21.9: Then the rākṣasī named Harijaṭā, whose eyes were like a cat's, opened her eyes wide in anger and spoke these words.
t.5.21.11: Why will you not take the status of wife to one who swells with valor, a hero who never turns back in battles, mighty and endowed with prowess?
t.5.21.13: Abandoning his inner palace, rich with a thousand women and adorned with many kinds of jewels, Rāvaṇa will come to you.
t.5.21.12: Abandoning his dear and highly esteemed wife, the most illustrious of all his women, the mighty king Rāvaṇa will come to you.
t.5.21.14: He by whom the gods, the Nāgas, Gandharvas and Dānavas were again and again conquered in war, on the field of battle, that very one has come to your side.
t.5.21.15: Why, O vile woman, do you not desire to become the wife of that great-souled Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, who is rich in every abundance?
t.5.21.16: He in fear of whom the sun does not scorch, and in fear of whom the wind does not blow, O long-eyed lady, why do you not stand by him?
t.5.21.18: O beautiful lady, why do you not set your mind on becoming the wife of Rāvaṇa, that king of the Nairṛtas, king of kings?
t.5.21.17: O fair-browed lady, he is the one for fear of whom the trees let fall showers of flowers, and the mountains and the clouds released water whenever he wished.
t.5.21.19: What has been told to you in truth is good, O lady, it is good, O beautiful one. Accept these words, O sweetly smiling one, or else you will cease to be.
